messages:
maria: Quick follow-up from last week's autoscale RFC: we need a clear split of responsibility between operator (on-node) and control plane for signals used in autoscaling decisions. thoughts?
aj: Operator should own fast safety checks (node health, gpu readiness, local prewarm cache) and emit primitives. Control plane should do policy (banking, global headroom).
derek: Strong +1. Also: operator needs to expose admission feedback synchronously (deny/accept with reason) not just metrics so control plane can make immediate routing decisions.
zoe: Admission API example idea:
```
POST /v1/pool/{pool_id}/admit
body: { tenant_bucket: 42, model_family: "mixtral-8x" }
response: { allowed: true, lane: "prewarm", estimated_warmup_ms: 3000 }
```
That keeps control plane from guessing.
maria: Good. Two followups: 1) what primitives must operator emit and at what latency? 2) what aggregated views must control plane compute?
henry: Minimum operator primitives: node_status (ready/cordoned), gpu_free_slots, prewarm_slots_reserved, warmup_inflight, last_model_load_ms, model_load_failures_total, eviction_events_total. Emit at 10s cadence and push event-on-change for critical events.
aj: Also expose a small per-pool cost_signal estimate (gpus_used_ratio * node_hourly_cost) so control plane can prefer cheaper pools for non-SLA traffic. Keep this coarse.
derek: Caveat: cost_signal requires cloud-tag sync and should be optional. Don't block MVP.
zoe: Aggregations control plane should do: headroom_deficit_1m/5m, fallback_rate_5m, warmup_p95_1h, tenant_spike_buckets. Control plane also keeps credit accounting for reserved tenants.
clair: For tenant spike detection: operator should emit sampled hashed_tenant_bucket warmup counts (e.g., bucket=0..255). No full tenant ids.
maria: Love that. Privacy preserved. What about label cardinality? keep labels to pool_id, model_family, zone, operator_version. No tenant labels except hashed bucket.
henry: Agree. Also telemetry format: compressed line-delimited JSON for events, prometheus metric names for counters/gauges. Example event:
```
{
  "ts":7712345678,
  "pool_id":"pool-east-2",
  "event":"model_load_start",
  "model":"mixtral-8x-q4",
  "attempt_ms_est":4200,
  "schema_v":2
}
```
Include schema_v so control plane can drop unknown shapes.
aj: Regarding aggregation: operator should keep short-term raw for 24h locally and only export aggregates (10s/1m summaries) upstream. But when a model_load_fail happens, push raw event immediately for debugging.
derek: Rollout safety: operator exposes operator_health_probe metric and operator_build tag. Control plane should ignore operators that fail to report for >30s during a rollout.
zoe: For autoscale decision-making: control plane runs two-tier logic: reactive (short window, aim latency) + predictive (longer window, smoothing, cost). Reactive uses operator primitives; predictive uses historical models.
maria: Do we want operator to implement any predictive logic (e.g., local short-term extrapolation) to reduce control plane noise?
henry: Keep operator dumb for now. Local extrapolation can mask systemic failures; prefer raw primitives and let control plane do the math.
clair: Ops note: sampling hashed tenant buckets will be implemented in the admission path; we should ensure sampling is uniform under high load.
aj: One more policy: when fallback_rate_5m > 0.5% for an SLA tenant, trigger immediate failover path and alert. Control plane will compute fallback_rate based on operator fallback_count metrics.
derek: Define metric names: redwood.dedicated.operator.gpu_free_slots (gauge), redwood.dedicated.operator.prewarm_reserved (gauge), redwood.dedicated.operator.warmup_inflight (gauge), redwood.dedicated.operator.model_load_failures_total (counter), redwood.dedicated.operator.fallback_count_total (counter).
zoe: Good. Also emit redwood.dedicated.operator.event_{name}_total for event counters, and redwood.dedicated.operator.health_probe (gauge 1/0).
maria: Action items: aj -> short API proto for admission endpoint, derek -> exact metric naming + units, zoe -> control-plane aggregation windows and alert thresholds, henry -> operator telemetry cadence and retention defaults, clair -> sampling strategy doc.
ops-bot: auto: meeting scheduled: "Autoscale signal interface sync" 2026-03-27 09:30 UTC (invitees: maria, aj, derek, zoe, henry, clair)
maria: Thanks all. I'll open a 1-page follow-up RFC with the admission API + minimal metrics list and we'll iterate. :rocket:
